gloss: it can't be helped; there's no way

definitions.gloss: it can't be helped; there's no way; oh well
definitions.explanation: Colloquial form of しかたがない. Expresses resignation or acceptance that nothing can be done about a situation.

definitions.gloss: can't help doing; can't stop oneself from
definitions.explanation: When preceded by a verb in て-form, expresses that one cannot help doing something.

examples.english: Oh well, what can you do.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しいんだから、しょうがないでしょ。
examples.english: I'm busy, so it can't be helped, right?

examples.japanese: {壊|こわ}れたのはしょうがない。{諦|あきら}めよう。
examples.english: It's broken, so there's nothing we can do. Let's move on.

examples.japanese: もう{終電|しゅうでん}がないからしょうがない。タクシーで{帰|かえ}ろう。
examples.english: There's no last train anymore, so it can't be helped. Let's take a taxi home.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}ばかりはしょうがない。{雨|あめ}でも{出|で}かけるしかない。
examples.english: There's nothing you can do about the weather. We have no choice but to go out even in the rain.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べたくてしょうがない。
{面白|おもしろ}くてしょうがない{本|ほん}を{見|み}つけた。
examples.english: I found a book that's so interesting I can't put it down.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}の{結果|けっか}が{気|き}になってしょうがない。
examples.english: I can't stop thinking about the game's result.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいゲームが{楽|たの}しくてしょうがないので、{毎日|まいにち}{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The new game is so much fun that I can't help playing it every day.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Contraction of しようがない (there's no way to do it)
{仕様|しよう} (way of doing) → しょう

VARIATIONS:
・しょうがない (common casual)
・しょうがねえ (rough/masculine speech)
・しょーがない (casual speech)

PATTERNS:
・〜てしょうがない = can't help but ~, unbearably ~
  Example: {食|た}べたくてしょうがない (dying to eat)
・〜でしょうがない (same meaning, after na-adjectives)

COMMON PHRASES:
・しょうがないなあ - oh well, what can you do (with a sigh)
・しょうがないやつだ - you're hopeless (affectionate criticism)

REGISTER:
Casual/colloquial. More common in everyday speech than しかたがない.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・しかたがない - standard/formal equivalent
・どうしようもない - there's nothing to be done (stronger)
・やれやれ - oh well, good grief (interjection)
